title: Rent Basis of the Late Fee: Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement Billing Note
content:
**Billing note.** For a Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement, the rent basis of the late fee is set by what the period was billed, and the late-fee percentage is applied once to that rent basis:

1. where the period's rent charge on the ledger is below the contracted monthly rent, the rent basis is that rent charge, as billed;
2. where the period's rent charge is not below the contracted monthly rent and a noticed rent change took effect on the period's due date, the rent basis is the rent in force before that change;
3. in every other case the rent basis is the contracted monthly rent.

The rent charge is the period's rent charge entry on the agreement's ledger. A noticed rent change took effect on the period's due date when the agreement's rent change history shows a change whose effective date is that due date; the rent in force before it is the rent before change that notice records.

## Decision table

| Period's rent charge compared with contracted rent | Rent change effective on the period's due date | Rent basis |
|---|---|---|
| below | any | the period's rent charge |
| not below | yes | the rent before that change |
| not below | no | the contracted monthly rent |

## Hypothetical cases

- First billing period charged $64.50 under a move-in discount, contracted rent $129.00: the rent basis is $64.50.
- A rent change from $120.00 to $132.00 effective on 10 April; the period due 10 April is charged $132.00 and the contracted rent is now $132.00: the rent basis is $120.00.
- A period charged $132.00, contracted rent $132.00, no rent change effective on its due date: the rent basis is $132.00.
- With a 15% late-fee percentage, those three bases give percentage figures of $9.675, $18.00 and $19.80 before any rounding.
